I then re-implemented V05 from the text, without the author's code. Account: plain sum of the ten chains, 157 FP server weeks of 2019-2021.

After that I read cv_stakes.py. Its conventions are the ones I had read from the text: exit_time <= cutoff, population sd, score on raw z, zero rule on the raw-R mean <= +0.02.

attacks.attack: Walk-forward integrity and truncation: 120 decisions (80 random out-of-fold chain decisions and 40 signals V05 sets to 0, seed 7); every fold also refitted from frames cut at its cutoff
attacks.result:
Decisions: own market and us100 cut at t_dec (plus one provisional bar). 0 descriptor mismatches (maximum difference 0.0); the stop distance equals 3 x ATR24 or 2 x A70 recomputed on the cut frame, exactly.

Fits rebuilt entirely on cut frames (orders, single-signal results, descriptors, the ten chains): 2020 and 2021 are identical to 0.0. 2019 is not: 671 training trades instead of 673. The 2 extra trades are brk72 btc (-1.49 R) and brk72 eth (-1.11 R), decided 2018-12-24 01:00 UTC. The Christmas closure moves their time exits to exactly 2018-12-25 00:00:00 UTC, which is the cutoff instant. The rule 'exit_time <= cutoff' therefore admits outcomes known AT the cutoff, not before it.

This is no look-ahead into the test year. It moves the 2019 coefficients by up to 0.003 and changes 2 of the 120 tested stakes. The author's test truncated tables built on full frames, so it could not see this.

Negative control: the price 2 minutes after t differs on the cut frame in 114 of 120 decisions (the other 6 are flat minutes). No global quantile and no descriptor using future bars was found.

conviction.notes:
The author's description is accurate and honest, and its numbers reproduce to the decimal. What I add:
- Criterion (a) sits on the bar: training on outcomes known strictly before the cutoff gives x1.1002 instead of x1.0951.
- Criterion (b) is fragile: 2019's +0.6 % turns negative with the Friday close, with the capped account and on top of K1.
- Criterion (f) can be argued either way, depending on whether the per-sleeve standardisations count as fitted parameters.
- The 2018 fold is negative.
- The zero rule removes trades that were winning on balance; the gain comes from the 1.5 stakes on high scores, mostly in 2020-2021.
- The gain largely overlaps K1.

Recommendation: do not carry V05 into the 2022-2025 look as it stands. For the user: in sample, about one tenth better per unit of swing, mostly from 2021, from betting 1.5 times on high-score crypto breakouts, and nothing left on a 1,000 EUR account at today's prices.

synth.growth_meaning:
Addendum I keeps nothing, so the gain per unit of swing is unchanged (x1.00) and so is the growth.

How to read a change in weekly Sharpe:
- At equal weekly swing, the mean weekly gain moves in proportion to the weekly Sharpe.
- A compounding account staked at a fixed fraction of its optimal (Kelly) stake grows at a rate proportional to the square of the Sharpe.
- At a fixed fall over a long horizon (expected deepest fall about stake x variance / mean), the stake can rise roughly in proportion to the Sharpe, so the gain rises roughly with its square.
- Over a short horizon such as one month, falls come from the swing. The stake cannot rise there, and the gain rises only in proportion to the Sharpe.
- In these samples the deepest fall at equal swing is noisy: K1+K2+K3 has a higher Sharpe but a deeper fall (24.1 R against 21.0 R).

For scale, all in sample and not kept from this addendum:
- V05 at x1.095 would mean about x1.20 in growth rate (x1.115 on top of K1).
- Addendum H's set K1+K2+K3 at x1.123 would mean about x1.26, mostly from 2019.

The user's demand is about 0.35 R per trade at today's noise, against 0.08 on 2022-2025 (task figure). That is a gain per unit of swing about 4.4 times today's, or about 19 times the growth rate at the same fraction of the optimal stake. After this addendum the whole gap remains. Staking by the odds does not close it; only better or more independent trades can.
synth.proposed_validation_look:
DECLARATION for the single look at 2022-2025 (PROTOCOL_V3 Addendum I, lead synthesis). Written 2026-11-12, before any 2022+ row is read by this synthesis, which reads none.

1. ADDENDUM I ADDS NO CHANGE. No conviction, clock or weight rule survived the criteria fixed in Addendum I and the attack, so none enters the look. FROZEN for Addendum I: every trade of every sleeve keeps a stake of 1 base stake (1 R). Nothing is fitted, so nothing is refitted on 1 January 2022, 2023, 2024 or 2025. V05 (the pooled crypto ridge, x1.095 in sample, below the x1.10 bar), IV00 and every other variant of the three lenses are excluded. None may be added to the look, before or after any 2022+ result.

2. THE ONE LOOK covers exactly the kept changes of Addendum H, each as declared by its synthesis, at most one change per sleeve.
- K1, K2 and K3, as declared in results/r2/autopsy/synthesis_B.json.
- K1: brk72_24h_wd ethusd skips a signal when 10,000 x stop_dist / P >= T(Y). T(2022) = 478.28 bp: the 2/3 quantile of the riskbp of the 2,345 in-sample signals decided before 2021-12-25, each taken alone with FP costs.
